thread:
ashok: Quick sync — I sketched an idea for adaptive per-route telemetry sampling that combines head/tail heuristics + route-tier signals. Goal: keep high-fidelity traces for SLO-sensitive routes and cheap aggregate coverage for low-tier ones. Thoughts? :thinking:

maria: high level sounds good. main worry is cost and retention complexity. customers already ask for 30d vs 90d tiers and we can't explode storage. do we have a migration path?

devon: i prototyped a simple scoring function yesterday. basic idea: route_score = alpha * error_rate + beta * p50_latency_norm + tier_weight. then pick head sample fraction = clamp(0.01, f(route_score), 1.0) and tail rules keep 100% of traces with error >= threshold. pseudo:```
// compute sampling fraction
score = 0.6*err_rate + 0.3*p50_norm + tier_weight[route] // tier_weight in [0,1]
frac = 0.01 + (score * 0.5) // scale to [0.01,0.51]
if is_error(trace) and trace.latency > latency_p95(route): keep_trace()
else sample_random(frac)
```

sre-liz: watch out for exporter backpressure. if tail rules suddenly retain lots of error traces for a busy route we saw the collector heap spike last time. need per-collector admission control and circuit-breakers. also consider soft-quotas per-account so a single noisy customer can't tilt storage.

ken: +1 to soft-quotas. also propose we tag spans with `route.tier` and `route.sampling_decision` so downstream pipelines (alerts, dashboards, billing) can adjust. tagging is cheap and makes retention+reingest decisions easier later.

maria: tagging helps, but we also need to expose effective sampling rate in console per-route. product wants to show "observability coverage: 35% (estimated)" next to each route. that requires us to persist counters from sampling decisions. lightweight counters only (no full traces).

ashok: agreed. plan to: 1) add route-level config (min_head_frac, max_head_frac, error_tail_threshold, tier_weight), 2) implement scorer in collector, 3) emit `sampling.counter.{route}` metrics to metrics pipeline, 4) attach tags to sampled spans. open questions: safe defaults? how fast do we adapt (window size)?

devon: for windowing i'd start with 5m rolling for score, 1m smoothing for frac changes to avoid flapping. safe defaults: min_head_frac=0.02, max_head_frac=0.5, error_tail_threshold=1% errors or status>=500.

sre-liz: also expose a kill-switch per-collector and a global fallback to uniform sampling when exporter lag > X. ops-bot will alert if collector-lag > 30s.

ops-bot: ALERT setup: collector_lag_seconds > 30 -> channel #eng-oncall, severity=high. logged rule id: telemetry-collector-lag-v1.

ken: one more UX thought — when customers use Dedicated, let them opt into a stricter head sampling (higher default) since they're paying for capacity. console toggle: "observability priority: cost-balanced | high-fidelity | custom" maps to tier_weight presets.

maria: agree. also need a migration doc for existing retention tiers. ops: can we simulate cost delta if we enable adaptive sampling for a busy customer? small export tool we can run on historical traces would help.

ashok: next steps: devon to submit PR with scorer + config schema, ken to add tags and metric names, maria to draft console UI copy for coverage and toggles, liz to draft collector admission-control proposal. let's reconvene in 48h. thanks all :thumbsup:
